notes.body: Texas auto insurers file their rates with the Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) and can charge them immediately. TDI reviews rates afterward and can disapprove ones that are inadequate, excessive, or unfairly discriminatory.
notes.title: File-and-use rates

notes.body: While rates are file-and-use, policy forms and endorsements must be approved by TDI before an insurer can use them.
notes.title: Policy forms need approval

notes.body: In a file-and-use system, market competition does most of the work keeping rates in check — which is exactly why comparing several carriers matters in Texas.
notes.title: Competition is the main rate regulator

sources: Texas Department of Insurance — Filings Made Easy Guide (May 2025)
Live Insurance News — Texas file-and-use explainer (Sept 2026)

minCoverage.notes: Texas is an at-fault state; PIP is optional, not required.
